category_title: Confident student with articulation-based Spoken Language Disorder
student_description: Helen is a confident kindergarten student with an articulation-related SLD who actively takes leadership roles in peer discussions and eagerly uses novel vocabulary. She uniquely requires an environment where her articulation errors are gently modeled rather than penalized, alongside explicit vocabulary instruction and structured peer-talk opportunities to foster her oral language development.

criteria.rationale: Helen thrives when given clear, child-friendly definitions and relatable examples of new words to use in her speech.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes explicitly teaching new vocabulary using child-friendly explanations, text connections, and relatable examples.

criteria.rationale: Helen is a confident leader who benefits from collaborative conversations to practice her oral language and newly acquired vocabulary.
criteria.check: The long-term plan incorporates planned, structured opportunities for peer-to-peer dialogue (such as turn-and-talks) to practice vocabulary.
